What Is Commercial Powder Coating?

Commercial powder coating is a dry finishing process in which electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto metal parts, then heated in an oven until it cures into a hard, even layer. It suits business orders where many parts must match, resist wear and ship on schedule.

The finish is made from thermoset powder, which cures with heat instead of drying like liquid paint. At a cure temperature of 180 to 200 °C, the powder flows, bonds to the metal and hardens into one continuous coating without runs or drips. As a form of commercial metal finishing, it replaces liquid paint where durability and repeatability matter. That makes it a dependable corrosion-resistant and chip-resistant choice for parts that face handling, weather and wear.

Typical customers send fabricated metal parts and commercial equipment components that must look alike from the first piece to the last. A commercial-grade finish should look the same on part one and part five hundred. Strong production powder coating depends on repeatable steps, so our commercial powder coating is planned around the whole order, starting from the bare metal. Our wider [powder coating services](/services) cover the full range of work we do.
Our Commercial Powder Coating Process

Our commercial powder coating process has six stages: intake and inspection, cleaning and pretreatment, masking, powder application, oven curing and final inspection. Each stage is documented so reorders match the first batch. The same controls support our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) work.
Step 1 – Intake and Inspection

We check each part for heavy rust, old coatings, weld quality and damage, then confirm the finish, quantity and delivery date for your order. We also plan racking so every surface can be reached and each load holds as many parts as it safely can.
Step 2 – Cleaning and Pretreatment

Parts are washed and chemically treated so the powder bonds to clean metal. Skipping this stage is a common reason finishes fail early. For more on this stage, see our [powder coating surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) page.
Step 3 – Masking and Plugging

Threads, bearing surfaces and mounting holes are protected before coating. Masking and plugging keep bolts turning and parts fitting, which matters when hundreds of identical parts must assemble without rework.
Step 4 – Electrostatic Powder Application
Charged powder is applied by electrostatic spray onto the grounded part, so it wraps around tubes, corners and recesses. This gives an even film across every piece in the run.
Step 5 – Oven Curing

Parts move into the curing oven, where commercial powder coating reaches temperature and hardens. Cure time depends on the powder and the mass of the part, so a heavy frame is planned differently from a small bracket.
Step 6 – Final Inspection and Handoff

We inspect the cured finish for coverage, adhesion and appearance. Typical orders are ready within 48 hours, and larger production runs are scheduled when we quote. We receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. We also record the colour and powder used, so a later order can repeat the finish exactly.
Our batch powder coating schedule keeps parts from waiting between steps, and for a tight lead time, tell us your date at quote.

Quality Standards for Commercial Powder Coating

Our commercial powder coating follows recognized standards: ASTM D3359 for adhesion, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance on every order. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request.

Quality starts at intake and ends at handoff. After curing, a good finish looks even in colour and gloss, with no thin spots, runs or bare edges. Edges, welds and recesses get particular attention because thin spots usually appear there. We flag any concern with you before parts leave the shop.

An adhesion test checks that the coating bonds to the metal. Dry film thickness readings confirm the coating is neither too thin to protect nor too thick to fit. The salt spray test measures corrosion resistance in a controlled chamber. It is a comparison tool rather than a promise of real-world life, so we explain what results mean for your commercial powder coating order.

Batch inspection means each load is checked before parts leave the shop, which keeps later deliveries consistent with the first. Careful production powder coating also depends on clean prep and correct curing, so every order follows the same documented steps. See our [certification](/certification) page for details.

Commercial Powder Coating FAQs

Short answer: we run commercial powder coating on metal parts in batches, with fast turnaround on typical orders. These answers cover order size, timing, repeat work, colour and logistics so you know what to expect before you book. Ask us anything else before you send parts.

blocks.q: How many parts can you coat in one order?
blocks.a: We coat orders from a few parts to large orders of matching pieces. Our capabilities page lists 6,000 lb capacity, so send quantity, dimensions and weight with your request and we will confirm how the order is batched.

blocks.q: How long does a bulk order take?
blocks.a: Typical commercial powder coating orders follow our 48-hour turnaround. Large or high-volume powder coating jobs are scheduled at quote based on quantity and part size. We receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.

blocks.q: Can you match the same colour on every reorder?
blocks.a: Yes. We record your colour and powder for each job so later batches match the first. Send a RAL code or a sample with your first order.

blocks.q: Can you set up recurring orders?
blocks.a: Yes. Tell us the part, quantity and timing at quote, and we plan racking and booking so each load is handled the same way.

blocks.q: Can one order include different part sizes?
blocks.a: Yes. We rack mixed parts so they cure well together, and heavier items are planned apart from small ones. List each part type with its quantity when you request a volume quote.

blocks.q: How do I get a quote for a large batch?
blocks.a: Send photos, dimensions, quantity and finish through our quote form. Pickup and delivery details are confirmed at quote based on your location, or you can drop parts off at 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, during opening hours.
